words.en_say: Mano po. A greeting where you touch an elder's hand to your forehead.

intro.title: Mano po 🙏
intro.desc: In the Philippines, kids show respect to grandparents, parents, aunts and uncles by taking their hand and touching the back of it to their own forehead. The elder says a blessing. Say "Mano po" when you do it!

stickers.desc: A soft, slightly sweet bread roll with a crumbly topping. Filipinos eat it warm for breakfast, often with butter or coffee.
A cold dessert of shaved ice, sweet beans, fruit and jelly, topped with ice cream. Halo-halo means "mix-mix", so you stir it all together before you eat it!
A banana wrapped in a thin pastry, fried, and coated in crunchy caramelized sugar.
A crispy fried roll filled with meat and vegetables. It is often served at parties with a dipping sauce.
A soft rice cake baked in a banana leaf and topped with cheese and coconut. It is a favorite at Christmas time.
Warm, silky soft tofu with sweet brown sugar syrup and little tapioca pearls. Street sellers carry it around in the morning.
A purple yam with bright purple flesh. It is used to make many sweet treats, like ice cream and cakes.
A young green coconut. You drink the fresh, sweet juice and eat the soft white coconut meat inside.
A sweet, juicy golden mango. Mangoes from the Philippines are famous around the world.
A smooth, creamy egg custard with sweet caramel sauce on top.
A small, soft, fluffy steamed rice cake, often topped with a slice of cheese.
A fluffy steamed bun filled with warm, savory meat. It is a popular snack or light meal.
Fried bananas coated in caramelized brown sugar and served on a stick.
Little fried balls of fish paste served on sticks with a sweet and tangy sauce. A popular street snack.
Filipino-style ice cream sold from colorful street carts, in flavors like ube, cheese and mango.
A crumbly little candy made of toasted flour, powdered milk and sugar, wrapped in colorful paper.
Crispy, crunchy fried pork skin, eaten as a salty snack.
Sweet corn on the cob, usually boiled. A popular snack in the Philippines.
Little boiled quail eggs dipped in bright orange batter and deep fried until crunchy.
A soft, buttery sweet bun topped with sugar and cheese.
A light, fluffy sponge cake that is so soft it melts in your mouth.
A soft, sweet milk candy rolled in sugar and wrapped in pretty cut paper.
Light, crunchy chips made from shrimp or fish. A crispy snack to share.
Chewy tapioca pearls in a cold, sweet drink with brown sugar syrup and jelly cubes.
A chewy, bouncy jelly made from cassava and rolled in grated coconut.
Sticky rice cooked in coconut milk and wrapped in banana or palm leaves. Peel off the leaf and eat!
A sweet, chewy sticky-rice cake with a sticky brown sugar and coconut milk topping.
A chewy, brown steamed rice cake, topped with fresh grated coconut.
Banana fritters: banana slices dipped in batter, fried, and dusted with sugar.
A tiny green citrus fruit that tastes like a sour lime. It is used in juice and squeezed over food.
A warm, creamy dessert soup made with coconut milk, sweet potatoes, bananas and tapioca pearls.
A soft, creamy pudding made from coconut milk and corn, topped with toasted coconut.
A soft sweet bread roll filled with sugary shredded coconut.
A smooth, sticky purple jam made from mashed purple yam. Sweet and creamy.
A colorful rice cake made of many sticky layers. "Sapin" means layer.
Crispy, flattened toasted rice flakes. They are sprinkled on desserts and chocolate drinks.
A sweet candy made of coconut strips cooked in brown sugar until chewy.
A soft candy made from sweet egg-yolk custard, rolled in sugar.
A soft, chewy cake made from cassava root, with a creamy custard topping.
Sticky rice and coconut wrapped in banana leaves and grilled over charcoal.
A warm porridge of rice cooked in broth, often topped with egg, toasted garlic and green onions.
Sticky rice cooked in chocolate until it is thick and sweet, often eaten for breakfast with milk poured on top.
Slices of sweet potato fried in brown sugar until crunchy and sticky, served on a stick.
A soft, chewy log made of rice flour and coconut milk, rolled in toasted rice flour.
A glowing star lantern made of bamboo and colorful paper, hung in Filipino windows every Christmas.
Purple sticky rice steamed in bamboo tubes, then topped with butter, coconut and brown sugar. Eaten after Simbang Gabi.
A sweet, glazed ham served at the Noche Buena feast on Christmas Eve.
A round cheese in red wax, a favorite on the Christmas table, often eaten with ham.
